content: This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before starting cycloserine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Cycloserine may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Cycloserine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. Cycloserine passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Lab and Medical Tests: While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as sputum tests, cycloserine blood levels, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts) should be conducted. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on how to safely discard the product. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is used in combination with other medications to treat tuberculosis (TB). In some cases, it may also be used to treat urinary tract infections (UTIs). This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking this medication (and other TB medications) for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear. Your doctor may also recommend taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) to help prevent certain side effects associated with cycloserine. Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, drowsiness, dizziness, or shaking (tremor). Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare.
